spec_match.rationale: Every capability claim is read from the live PerformanceObserver.supportedEntryTypes on each thread rather than from documentation, and the main-thread entry shown is a real one produced by blocking this page — its scripts array, blockingDuration and renderStart are the browser's values.

interactive.rationale: A live side-by-side of both threads' entry types with a button that blocks the main thread and prints the resulting entry; a worker blocker with three witnesses and a continuous round-trip ping log; and a comparison page that blocks the worker and shows what its self-timer caught against the ten fields a real entry carries.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index leads on the blind spot — work is moved to a worker because it is heavy, and heavy work is what blocks event loops — which is the feature's own motivation, and states up front that the pages measure the gap rather than the fix.

edge_cases.rationale: Covers the self-timer's two failure modes explicitly: a stall that does not straddle two of its ticks, and several short blocks that each fall under the threshold while adding up to an unresponsive worker. Also handles a main thread without long-animation-frame at all, and a block that produces no entry because the page is not being rendered.

references.rationale: chromestatus.com/feature/5387465121726464 on the index and all three concept pages, with the W3C specification, Chrome for Developers documentation and MDN.

conformance.rationale: Six immutable assertions: PerformanceObserver exists; the main thread supports the entry type; a real main-thread entry carries a scripts array; a dedicated worker lists long-animation-frame (the feature, expected to fail before 153); a worker's block produces no main-thread entry (the blind spot the demos rest on); and performance.now plus setTimeout are available inside a worker so the workaround can exist.

runtime_evidence.rationale: deno task drive over all three pages in real Chrome 150: 3/3, 20 assertions. Measured: the main thread lists 13 entry types including long-animation-frame, a worker lists exactly three — mark, measure, resource — with and without --enable-experimental-web-platform-features. Blocking the main thread for 250ms produced a 252ms entry with 202ms blocking duration and one attributed script; blocking the worker for 400ms produced nothing from either observer while the round-trip ping went from 1.8ms to 360ms.

telemetry_health.rationale: Each page emits showcaseTelemetry.assert with the measured entry-type counts, block durations, observed entry counts and worst ping.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables throughout, no raw colour literals, buttons set background and colour, 44px control minimums, and every wide table in its own scroll container.

accessibility.rationale: The ping log is role=log with an accessible name; witness cards are articles labelled by their headings with a text answer as well as a border colour; results are announced through aria-live; the entry-type chips carry a strike-through and a class rather than colour alone for the absent ones.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Thread and witness grids are auto-fit minmax and stack at 360px; the entry-type chip lists wrap; the comparison and entry tables scroll inside their own containers.

openQuestions.title: Re-run on a browser that has the feature and show a worker entry
openQuestions.detail: Every page branches on the live supported-types list, so the day a worker reports long-animation-frame the blocking demo's first witness turns green and the comparison page says the workaround is redundant. What has never been exercised is that branch — it has only ever been reasoned about — so the first run on Chrome 153 is a real test of these pages, not a formality.

openQuestions.title: Demonstrate the multiple-short-blocks failure mode rather than describing it
openQuestions.detail: The hand-rolled page explains that four 100ms tasks defeat a 50ms-threshold self-timer while leaving a worker unresponsive for 400ms. That is the most interesting thing on the page and it is currently prose. A control that runs N blocks of M milliseconds and shows the self-timer recording nothing would make it a measurement, and it would still be true after the feature ships.

guidanceConsulted.query: live region for a streaming log of timings
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Give an append-only log role=log and an accessible name so a screen reader announces new entries without re-reading the whole region.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The ping log is role=log with aria-label; each round trip is appended as its own element, and the summary that follows is a separate aria-live output so the conclusion is announced once rather than per ping.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: deno task drive counts the appended log children and asserts the summary text.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive comparison cards that stack without horizontal overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Auto-fit grids with intrinsic minimums; wide tabular content in its own scroll container.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Thread and witness grids use repeat(auto-fit, minmax(230–260px, 1fr)) with align-content:start; the ten-row comparison table and the entry-field table both sit in overflow-x:auto wrappers.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: responsive-check desktop + mobile on the feature.

summary: Three concepts about an absence, built so the absence is measured rather than asserted: a worker lists three entry types where the main thread lists thirteen, and a 400ms worker stall is reported by nobody while a ping quietly goes from 2ms to 360ms. Building it exposed two real ordering bugs in the demo's own worker — a reset that erased the gap it was meant to record, and a report that raced ahead of the timer tick that would have found it.
